title: Sri Lanka’s flawless display pleases Coach Ratnayake | Daily FT
summary:
Friday, 27 November 2026 00:06
-     - 16

The champion Sri Lanka Women’s team with Head Coach Rumesh Ratnayake (centre) and support staff

Sri Lanka finished as champions of the ICC Women’s Emerging Nations Trophy 2026 after a flawless fortnight in Ajman, winning all eight of their matches to claim the title for the first time and succeed inaugural winners Thailand.

The second edition of the tournament brought together 10 teams for 30 matches from 12 to 25 November at the Karwan Sports Club Cricket Ground and Seven Districts Sports Club. Vishmi Gunaratne was named Player of the Tournament after finishing as the leading run-scorer with 324 runs, while Sathya Sandeepani shared top spot among the wicket-takers with 17, capped by four for 13 in Wednesday’s six-wicket win over Ireland in the final.

Sri Lanka topped Group A with four wins from four. They then beat Zimbabwe and the Netherlands by nine wickets each and edged Pakistan by four runs to finish top of the Super Six with 10 points.

Ireland finished third in Group A and carried no points into the Super Six. However, wins over Pakistan by nine wickets, Zimbabwe by three wickets, and the Netherlands by 44 runs lifted them to second place and a spot in the final.

Scotland, Pakistan, and the Netherlands finished level on four points in the Super Six, with Scotland third on net run rate, while Zimbabwe came sixth. Hosts United Arab Emirates (UAE), Papua New Guinea (PNG), Bangladesh, and defending champions Thailand bowed out after the group stage.

“We approached this tournament as seriously as we could. We had played Ireland and Scotland before, but the other teams were relatively unknown, so we made sure we watched and analysed them, and went about our business as we would against any nation above us,” said Sri Lanka Women’s Head Coach Rumesh Ratnayake.

“In the past, we have got our planning right but not our execution, especially with the ball, so that was our focus here. I’m very pleased with the manner in which the team went about the tournament from start to finish. We have a good foundation to build on as we approach a very important series against Australia.”

Sri Lanka’s winning Captain Harshitha Samarawickrama said that she was happy with the result because it was a team effort.

“Everyone in the team knew their roles going into the match, and they did really well throughout the series. The facilities throughout the tournament at both venues were good. We took it one game at a time and performed well as a team, so we’re looking forward to more tours. The Associate nations producing such performances at the tournament is a good thing for the women’s game,” she said.

Ireland’s losing Captain Gaby Lewis said: “We were confident coming into the game but we underperformed on the day. That being said, this whole tournament has been a real positive for us, and there are lots of learnings we can take from it. Being put in to bat first, we could have adapted better, but that’s something we can learn from.”

title: MCC Laws of Cricket introduced in Sinhala and Tamil | Daily FT
summary:
Friday, 27 November 2026 00:04
-     - 15

MCC Head of Cricket Fraser Stewart (right) speaks to the media in the presence of SLC Umpire Education Senior Manager Lyndon Hannibal and SLC Cricket Committee Chairman Sidath Wettimuny

The Marylebone Cricket Club (MCC), in collaboration with Sri Lanka Cricket (SLC), has translated the MCC Laws of Cricket into Sinhala and Tamil, enabling cricketers at all levels across Sri Lanka to read the Laws in their native language.

The initiative will also help umpires, match officials, media personnel and other stakeholders deepen their understanding of the Laws of the game.

The translation project began following a request from the International Cricket Council (ICC) to SLC to make the MCC Laws of Cricket available in Sinhala and Tamil.

SLC’s umpire educators will use the translations across all nine provinces to teach, examine and mentor umpires in both languages, opening pathways into officiating for more men and women across the island.

The project was completed with the approval of MCC, which has been the custodian of the Laws of Cricket since its foundation in 1787.

MCC’s Laws Sub-Committee is responsible for debating, reviewing and drafting the Laws, with changes subject to approval by MCC’s Main Committee.

The completion of the translations was announced yesterday at a media briefing held at Sri Lanka Cricket.

The briefing was attended by SLC Cricket Committee Chairman Sidath Wettimuny, MCC Head of Cricket Fraser Stewart and SLC Umpire Education Senior Manager Lyndon Hannibal.

Stewart will conduct a workshop for SLC umpires on the Laws of Cricket, with particular emphasis on recent changes. The session will give Sri Lankan umpires an opportunity to learn directly from a representative of the custodian of the laws.

title: Sineth (105), Croospulle (116) power Sri Lanka ‘A’ to final | Daily FT
summary:
Friday, 27 November 2026 00:04
-     - 24

Lasith Croospulle and Sineth Jayawardena slammed centuries apiece as Sri Lanka ‘A’ beat India ‘A’ by eight wickets in a phenomenal run chase to enter the final of the Asia Cup Rising Stars (50-over) tournament in the first semi-final played at Doha yesterday.

Sri Lanka ‘A’ will meet the winner of the second semi-final between Pakistan ‘A’ and Bangladesh ‘A’ today, in the final scheduled for Sunday.

Chasing 318, Sri Lanka ‘A’ hunted down the target losing just two wickets and with 9.5 overs to spare which showed how dominant they were. It was a clinical display of hitting by the Lankan batsmen who didn’t put a foot wrong in their run chase.

Jayawardena led the charge against Arshad Khan with a big over, and, from then on, runs started to flow. Croospulle was happy to play second-fiddle to Jayawardena in the opening partnership of 174 off 129 balls. The openers both reached their hundreds. Player of the Match Jayawardena scored 105 off 70 balls (10 fours, 6 sixes) and made India ‘A’ pay dearly for dropping him on nought off his first ball by Tanush Kotian at backward point. Croospulle made 116 off 107 balls (12 fours, 3 sixes). Following Jayawardena’s dismissal, Croospulle, joined by Nishan Madushka, added a further 91 off 83 balls to dent the India ‘A’ bowling further.

Madushka chipped in with his third consecutive fifty – 58* off 56 balls (5 fours, 1 six), while skipper Pavan Rathnayake (31* off 16 balls, 1 four, 3 sixes) got off the mark with a positive intent with a six. They made light work of the chase, remaining unflustered throughout their partnership of 53* off 37 balls. The intent remained positive going for their shots and tearing apart the bowling. The knocks at the top were absolutely majestic, full of elegant and eye-catching strokes. India weren’t incisive or threatening enough with the ball. Their pace battery struggled, and Sri Lanka were head and shoulders above their opponents.

Winning the toss and batting first, India ‘A’ put up a healthy total of 317-8. Vaibhav Sooryavanshi came out all guns blazing but fell for 40 out of an opening stand of 80 off 48 balls with Abhishek Sharma, who raced to his 50 off 37 balls and batted fluently for his 78 off 63 balls (11 fours, 1 six). Following the dismissal of Sooryavanshi, the India ‘A’ run rate dropped, with Wanuja Sahan and Janith Liyanage tightening the screws.

At one point when Abhishek and Varma were going strong, India ‘A’ looked to be aiming at something close to 350 plus, but were held back by the Lankan spinners. From 197-2, they slipped to 235-6 between overs 30-40. However, Shahbaz Ahmed (54* off 48 balls, 4 sixes) and Tanush Kotian (28) ensured they didn’t lose their way completely, adding 73 off 55 balls to give India ‘A’ a total to defend.

Sri Lanka ‘A’ were well below par in the field, spilling catches, missing multiple run-out chances, and leaking boundaries, even as their spinners pulled things back in the middle overs. But in the end, their batters compensated for those lapses on the field.

Scores: 

India ‘A’ 317-8 (50) (Vaibhav Sooriyavanshi 40, Abhishek Sharma 78, Tilak Varma 53, Kumar Kushagra 21, Shahbaz Ahmed 54*, Tanush Kotian 28, Ravindu Fernando 2/60, Janith Liyanage 2/37)

Sri Lanka ‘A’ 318-2 (41.3) (Lasith Croospulle 116, Sineth Jayawardena 105, Nishan Madushka 58*, Pavan Rathnayake 31*)

title: 11 Bangladeshi players in 2027 IPL auction list; Shakib, Mustafizur missing | Daily FT
summary:
Friday, 27 November 2026 00:02
-     - 14

Former captain Shakib Al-Hasan and fast bowler Mustafizur Rahman are notable absentees on the list of 11 Bangladeshi cricketers who have registered for the Indian Premier League’s (IPL) upcoming player auction, as tensions continue to simmer between the South Asian neighbours.

Top-order batter Towhid Hridoy leads the players, named on a list released on Wednesday, who are seeking a place in the world’s most lucrative cricket franchise league, a year after Mustafiz’s controversial removal from the IPL.

The 11 Bangladeshis feature on an initial list of 1,220 players for the December 16 mini auction in Goa, although the pool will be trimmed before franchises make their selections, the Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) said.

“With 184 players already retained or picked by the franchises ahead of the auction, a maximum of 66 slots, including 25 overseas slots, are available to be filled,” the BCCI said in a statement.

Apart from Hridoy, who is enjoying great run-scoring form, Hasan Mahmud, Parvez Hossain Emon, Ripon Mondol, Rishad Hossain, Saif Hassan, Shak Mahedi Hasan, Shamim Hossain, Shoriful Islam, Tanzim Hasan Sakib, and Taskin Ahmed are on the list, according to cricket news outlet Cricinfo.

The presence of Bangladeshi names on the draft auction comes as a surprise, months after the country’s expulsion from the ICC Men’s T20 World Cup, cohosted by India.

The Bangladesh Cricket Board (BCB) refused to send its team to India over security concerns, which followed a fallout over star pacer Mustafizur’s removal from the Kolkata Knight Riders’ roster upon the BCCI’s instructions.

The relationship between India and Bangladesh remains tense over Dhaka’s extradition request for Hasina, which New Delhi has yet to comply with.

title: Clive Lloyd tips Test Twenty youngsters for international cricket | Daily FT
summary:
Friday, 27 November 2026 00:01
-     - 15

Clive Lloyd

Inaugural Test Twenty at SSC

Former West Indies captain Sir Clive Lloyd believes most of the young cricketers taking part in the inaugural Test Twenty tournament at the SSC grounds will go on to represent their countries.

“Most of them will play for their country,” said Lloyd, who led West Indies to World Cup titles in 1975 and 1979 and is mentoring Europe at the tournament.

Lloyd said the questions he fielded from the players, some as young as 13, had made as much of an impression on him as their cricket.

“I spoke to the captains yesterday and the questions were very intelligent. It’s obvious that they want to learn,” he said. “I still speak to a lot of them at breakfast and social gatherings, and they are very, very knowledgeable.”

Founded by Gaurav Bahirvani, Test Twenty has brought together 160 boys and girls aged 13 to 21. They represent four teams; South Asia, Australasia, Europe and Sub-Saharan Africa, in a format that combines the scores of the boys’ and girls’ sides to determine the match resul

Lloyd, who also serves as a founding board adviser, said he had worked with Bahirvani before and wanted to be involved once he heard what the tournament would offer young players.

“This is a game that has given me my upward mobility and a wonderful life,” he said. “And to see a 13-year-old and a 14-year-old asking you some very searching questions, I am sure they are on the right track.”

Lloyd said playing overseas gave youngsters the chance to experience different cultures, form friendships and test themselves against players they might otherwise never meet.

“The best thing about playing and going overseas is the friends you make. The friends you make in cricket, you make them for life,” he said. “They are enjoying themselves, and at this stage in their lives, I am sure they will remember these moments and want to go and play cricket to a higher standard.”

Lloyd will present the trophy to the inaugural champions. He said the adults guiding the players had a responsibility to teach them how to conduct themselves on the field.

“It is up to the managers, captains and all those in leadership positions to pass on the right knowledge to our young cricketers,” he said. “Let’s give young people a chance to prove that they have understood the game.”

title: Sinner ruled out of 2027 Australian Open after knee surgery | Daily FT
summary:
Friday, 27 November 2026 00:00
-     - 12

Jannik Sinner

World number two Jannik Sinner was yesterday ruled out of the 2027 Australian Open in January as he recovers from right knee surgery.

The Italian, who won the season-opening Grand Slam in 2024 and 2025, announced this week that he had gone under the knife at a clinic in Finland.

He has not played a match since winning Wimbledon for the second time in July, with his appearance at Melbourne Park always in doubt.

The 25-year-old Sinner was having a brilliant campaign before being stopped by his knee problem, with five Masters 1000 titles alongside his triumph at Wimbledon.

The Italian’s 94% win record in 2026 was the best of his career.

In his absence, Alexander Zverev has taken over as world number one.

title: Browns Hotels and Resorts makes its mark in sustainable hospitality with multiple national accolades | Daily FT
summary:
Friday, 27 November 2026 00:03
-     - 14

Browns Hotels and Resorts has earned national recognition at two prominent award ceremonies in 2026 for its continued commitment to environmental responsibility and sustainable hospitality. 

Two of its coastal properties, The Calm Resort and Spa in Pasikudah and Dickwella Resort and Spa, received accolades at the Presidential Environment Awards and National Cleaner Production Awards 2026.

At the Presidential Environment Awards 2026, held at the Bandaranaike Memorial International Conference Hall (BMICH), Colombo, The Calm Resort and Spa received a Bronze Award, while Dickwella Resort and Spa was presented with a Merit Award in the Industry Sector – Hotels Type A and B category. Further strengthening this achievement, both properties were also recognised at the National Cleaner Production Awards 2026 in the Service Sector – Hotel Medium Category, acknowledging their efforts towards adopting cleaner production practices and integrating greater environmental responsibility into their operations.

Together, these recognitions highlight the practical measures undertaken at both properties to minimise their environmental footprint while maintaining responsible hospitality operations. Initiatives spanning energy efficiency, responsible water consumption, waste management, coastal conservation and community engagement form part of their ongoing efforts to operate more sustainably.

The achievements at both properties reflect the leadership and commitment of Sujeewa Basnayake, General Manager of The Calm Resort and Spa, and Sisira Senaratne, General Manager of Dickwella Resort and Spa, together with their respective teams.

Browns Hotels and Resorts CEO Eksath Wijeratne said: “For Browns Hotels and Resorts, sustainability is an ongoing journey, shaped by a shared responsibility to create positive change today while safeguarding the destinations and communities that future generations will experience. While these national recognitions are a proud milestone for our Group, what matters most is the progress they represent.”

These property-level initiatives are also part of a broader sustainability vision taking shape across Browns Hotels and Resorts through BIGG CARE, the Group’s sustainability framework built around Green Governance, Climate Action, Accountability, Resource Efficiency and Engagement. Recently, the Group took another significant step in formalising this commitment with the launch of its Sustainability Programme and Policy, establishing a more structured approach to embedding responsible practices across its operations.

Browns Hotels and Resorts Assistant Manager – Sustainability and CSR Prabuddha Siriwardhana said: “Sustainability becomes meaningful when commitments translate into everyday practices. Through BIGG CARE, we are working towards bringing greater accountability and consistency to our sustainability efforts across the Group. Our focus now is to build on this momentum and continue driving measurable improvements across our operations.”

Located along the shores of Pasikudah, The Calm Resort and Spa offers 70 rooms and suites, complemented by its tranquil coastal setting and experiences inspired by the East Coast. Dickwella Resort and Spa, set on a picturesque peninsula along Sri Lanka’s southern coastline, features 76 rooms and suites, offering guests a range of coastal experiences shaped by its spectacular ocean surroundings. 

Across its portfolio, Browns Hotels and Resorts remains focused on promoting conscious operations, responsible resource management and meaningful engagement with local communities, while contributing to the long-term preservation of Sri Lanka’s natural environment.

title: Uga Resorts earns three top rankings at 2026 Condé Nast Traveller Readers’ Choice Awards | Daily FT
summary:
Friday, 27 November 2026 00:02
-     - 12

Uga Prāva

Uga Ulagalla

Uga Halloowella

Uga Resorts has earned notable recognition in the 2026 Condé Nast Traveller Readers’ Choice Awards, with three its properties ranked among the leading hotels and resorts in the Rest of Asia Category. 

Uga Prāva claimed top honours as number one among the region’s best hotels with a score of 98.82, while Uga Haloowella took eighth place with a score of 91.24. Simultaneously, Uga Ulagalla was ranked sixth among the region’s best resorts scoring 97.28.

Published in the November 2026 issue of Condé Nast Traveller, the annual Readers’ Choice Awards are designed to celebrate outstanding travel experiences as voted for by readers. The results are a testament to the diversity of Uga Resorts’ portfolio, which brings together Sri Lanka’s beaches, hill country heritage and cultural richness through distinctive hospitality experiences. 

Locate along the coast in Tangalle, Uga Prāva was voted the number one hotel in the Rest of Asia category. Featuring seven suites, the property offers a cozy, intimate stay that combines contemporary minimalist design with the natural beauty of the Indian Ocean. Notable highlights include the infinity pool, considered wellness experiences and dining shaped by the daily catch and other local sourced ingredients.

The property also offers guests an opportunity to explore the country’s southern coastline, with experiences such as whale watching, snorkelling, visits to ancient temples, and encounters with the regions picturesque natural landscape. The top ranking is attributed to Uga Prāva’s distinctive approach to luxury, which is centred on thoughtful design, tranquillity and strong connection with its surroundings. 

Uga Halloowella, which secured eighth position, is nestled in the hills of Hatton, overlooking the Castlereagh Reservoir. 

Established in 1880, the historic estate was restored by Uga in collaboration with reputed architect Channa Daswatte. Situated 1,444 metres above sea level, the colonial bungalow is surrounded by lush tea plantations and combines historic character with contemporary comforts. 

The property features six luxurious suites, refined dining, expansive laws and an infinity pool, creating an intimate retreat amidst the enduring charm of the hill country. The recognition reflects Uga Hallowella’s preservation of its architectural heritage and its ability to provide distinct experiences for the modern traveller. 

Uga Ulagalla secured sixth place in the Best Resorts in Rest of Asia category. This recognition is attributed to its distinct combination of heritage, seclusion and nature-led luxury. Set among 58 acres of paddy fields and ancient woodland in Sri Lanka’s Cultural Triangle, the property occupies an estate with deep historical roots. Featuring 25 standalone villas, each with a private plunge pool, Uga Ulagalla offers guests an intimate experience among landscape of reservoirs ponds and greenery. 

The heart of the estate is the 150-year-old house, which was once the residence of the village chieftain. Today, the manor is the centre point for dining and gathering, combining historic architecture and contemporary hospitality. The resort also offers access to some of Sri Lanka’s most significant cultural attractions, including ancient ruins, monumental dagobas and UNESCO World Heritage sites, providing a distinctive base from which to explore the island’s history.

The three rankings represent a significant achievement for Uga Resorts and reinforce Sri Lanka’s presence on the international luxury travel landscape. From Uga Prāva’s intimate coastal setting to Uga Halloowella’s historic hill country retreat and Uga Ulagalla’s heritage-rich wilderness, each property offers a distinct interpretation of Sri Lankan hospitality.

Recognition across both hotel and resort categories highlights the breadth of experiences available to international travellers and the appeal of properties that draw on their natural surroundings, cultural identity and heritage to create memorable stays.

title: Hunas River opens in Balapitiya | Daily FT

Head of Hunas Hospitality Rajith Gooneratne

Hunas Hospitality marked the opening of Hunas River Balapitiya on 14 November, introducing a five-bedroom riverside retreat and the collection’s first property in the luxury boutique segment. Formerly known as The River House Balapitiya, the property is set within a 12-acre estate featuring cinnamon, jackfruit and cashew trees.

Each of the five bedrooms has been individually styled. One features a private pool, while two have outdoor Jacuzzis. Personalised butler service and curated dining are central to the guest experience.

In his welcome address, Head of Hunas Hospitality Rajith Gooneratne described the property’s focus as “an intimate and personalised guest experience, where attention to detail, exceptional service, and the beauty of the surrounding environment come together to create something truly memorable.”

The opening also highlighted the contribution of the group’s Japanese partners. Speaking at the event, Watanabe-san said, “I strongly believe in the future of Sri Lankan tourism, and through our partnership, we hope to play a meaningful role in supporting its development and showcasing Sri Lanka to the world.”

Speaking on behalf of CCH, Tanabe-san said, “It has been an absolute pleasure collaborating with such a dedicated and passionate team, and I believe this partnership holds great promise for the future.”

Hunas Hospitality is the Sri Lankan hotel collection of Hunas Holdings PLC and is managed by Hunas Leisure. Its hospitality roots date back to 1971, when Hunas Falls opened. The collection includes Hunas Falls in Elkaduwa and Hunas Beach and Hunas River in Balapitiya. Across its hill country, beachfront and riverside properties, the collection focuses on personalised service and experiences shaped by the character of each setting.
